description: Clear password-reset SOP, faithful and complete skill
source: IT SOP: Reset a locked-out user account. When a user is locked out, support must: 1) Confirm the request arrived as a helpdesk ticket — never act on chat or phone alone; the ticket is the audit trail. 2) Verify identity: match requester email to the ticket and confirm one secondary detail (employee ID or manager name). 3) Trigger the reset: run `idm reset <email>`, which emails a one-time link valid for 30 minutes. 4) Tell the user to set a policy-compliant password (14+ chars, not reused from the last 5). 5) Close the ticket noting who was verified. Hard rule: never reset without a verified ticket; escalate to security if an account is reset more than twice in one week.

source: Runbook: rolling back a bad production deploy. When error rate exceeds 5% for 3 minutes after a deploy: 1) Announce in #incidents that you are rolling back. 2) Run `deploy rollback --to-last-green` to restore the previous green build. 3) Confirm error rate returns below 1% within 5 minutes. 4) If rollback does not recover, page the on-call SRE. Never hotfix forward during an active incident — always roll back first.

source: Support policy: processing a customer refund. Never issue a refund past 30 days without manager approval.
